items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: It’s like Joe Morello told me one time

ctx.x: Yeah. What do you tell your, with jazz majors, what do you advise to them as far as post- graduation and making a living?

Swing or I’ll kill you. No, no, it’s just old jokes, sorry. Old musicians will remember that old joke. It’s like Joe Morello told me one time, he said, “A lot of times you can’t remember how many bars there are to a tune, but the old musicians can remember how many tunes there are to a bar” and I left my cowbell down on the campus, God-dog it.

items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I used to do small little pockets of tributes to Joe Morello, and throw some of those in there.

ctx.x: One of my drum students, Tom Harden, who was in the percussion section said, “man that guy set such an energy level.”

Well I used to do a, thank you very much, I used to do a number of things, I tried to be original, with Brubeck, but as you know, every single night we would sooner or later we’d have to close with “Take Five.” They just would not let him out of town without playing “Take Five,” and so that was my big moment and I used to do small little pockets of tributes to Joe Morello, and throw some of those in there.
I wonder, I always wondered how Brubeck felt about that, that he was such a writer but the band’s biggest hit, you know, he didn’t write.
